report.summary: Chunk 2 defines closed vocabularies (CANARY_STATUSES, SEVERITIES, FAILING_STATUSES), constants, and the nonce function. All claims are verifiable within this chunk or marked uncheckable.
risks: FAILING_STATUSES | low | Excludes 'unavailable' deliberately, but if any logic elsewhere treats 'unavailable' as a failure, inconsistency may arise. | Audit all code referencing FAILING_STATUSES to confirm 'unavailable' is handled separately.

REPLY_TRIM = 400 | medium | Hard-coded trim length may truncate meaningful content in replies, potentially losing evidence. | Verify that 400 characters is sufficient for all probe types; consider making configurable.
TRAILING_WINDOW = 20 | low | Hard-coded window size may be too short or too long for some use cases, affecting median comparison accuracy. | Evaluate if window should be configurable or adaptive.
SLOWER_RATIO and SLOWER_ABS_S | low | Thresholds hard-coded; may need tuning per environment. | Consider making these configurable or documenting rationale.

handoff.purpose: Define closed vocabularies, constants, and nonce generation.

symbols.name: CANARY_STATUSES
symbols.note: Tuple of five status strings: ok, wrong_answer, timeout, unavailable, error.

symbols.name: SEVERITIES
symbols.note: Tuple of two severity strings: liveness, quality.

symbols.name: FAILING_STATUSES
symbols.note: Frozenset of statuses that count as failure: wrong_answer, timeout, error.

symbols.name: VENDOR_KEYS
symbols.note: Tuple of four vendor key strings: anthropic, openai, google, local.

symbols.name: new_nonce
symbols.note: Returns a string like 'K7F3A9C1' (starts with 'K' + 7 hex digits).

symbols.name: _rng
symbols.note: Returns a random.Random seeded from the nonce string.

claims.text: Outcome of one probe. CLOSED -- nothing may invent a sixth, and in particular ``unavailable`` and ``wrong_answer`` are separate members because a report that merges them is a report that lies.
claims.why: The tuple has exactly five members; unavailable and wrong_answer are distinct.

claims.text: ok -- we asked, and the deterministic checker accepted the reply
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the checker logic; cannot verify that 'ok' corresponds to acceptance.

claims.text: wrong_answer -- we asked, the bytes came back, the checker REJECTED them
timeout -- we asked and nothing came back inside the budget
unavailable -- WE COULD NOT ASK (not installed, not signed in, asleep)
error -- the transport itself failed (bad response, nonzero exit, over-budget prompt, secret-floor refusal)
A probe either measures whether the lane is ALIVE and the bytes arrived, or whether the lane's reasoning is the right SHAPE.
claims.why: SEVERITIES tuple contains exactly 'liveness' and 'quality', consistent with the claim.

claims.text: Only ``liveness`` trips the exit code -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: No exit code logic in this chunk; module docstring not present.

claims.text: Statuses that mean 'we asked and it did not work'. ``unavailable`` is deliberately absent: we never asked, so there is nothing to have failed.
claims.why: FAILING_STATUSES is frozenset({'wrong_answer', 'timeout', 'error'}); 'unavailable' is not included.
No history writing logic in chunk.

claims.text: Cheapest sensible local model. This runs often; the 32b is not a health check, it is a bill.
claims.why: Value is 'qwen2.5-coder:7b', a 7B model, consistent with 'cheapest sensible' and not 32b.

claims.text: Vendor keys, spelled the way the operator types them (same set as ``council.session.VENDOR_KEYS`` so ``--vendors`` means one thing repo-wide).
claims.why: Cannot verify against council.session.VENDOR_KEYS; not in chunk.

claims.text: How much of a reply is kept on the record. Enough to see what a lane actually said, not enough to turn history.jsonl into a transcript store.
claims.why: Value 400 is a moderate trim; claim is a design intent, not a testable fact.

claims.text: Trailing window for the median comparison. Long enough to be a baseline, short enough that a lane which legitimately got faster stops being compared against last month.
claims.why: Value 20 is a reasonable window; claim is design intent.

claims.text: A lane counts as materially slower only if it is BOTH a large multiple of its median AND absolutely slow enough for a human to care. Either test alone cries wolf: a 0.2s -> 0.6s local hop is 3x and means nothing.
claims.why: SLOWER_RATIO=2.0 and SLOWER_ABS_S=2.0 enforce both conditions; example matches.
Function returns 'K' + 7 hex digits, e.g., 'K7F3A9C1' is possible.

claims.text: Fresh PER PROBE PER LANE, not per run: a reused nonce cannot distinguish a lane that answered from a lane (or a cache, or a shared transcript) that echoed somebody else's answer -- which is the exact confusion the anchoring incident was made of.
claims.why: No usage context; claim about nonce uniqueness policy cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Deterministic per-nonce randomness, so ``build`` and ``check`` agree.
claims.why: Function seeds random.Random with nonce string; deterministic given same nonce.

observations.what: CANARY_STATUSES is a tuple of five strings; docstring says 'CLOSED -- nothing may invent a sixth'.
new_nonce returns string of length 8 (prefix 'K' + 7 hex chars).
_rng uses secrets.token_hex(4).upper()[:7] which produces 7 uppercase hex digits; note token_hex(4) yields 8 hex digits, but slicing to 7 shortens it.
DEFAULT_OLLAMA_MODEL is 'qwen2.5-coder:7b', a 7B model, not 32b as mentioned in docstring.
